Certain things set me off in a way that feels…bigger than it should be. Getting emails about bills or seeing the old company’s logo online makes my chest tighten and I feel this wave of dread, like I’m right back in that office being told to pack my things. Even small reminders—someone mentioning layoffs on the news—can leave me on edge for the rest of the day.

What’s really bothering me are these strange experiences I’ve had, mostly at night but a couple of times during the day too. I’ll hear someone say my name, clear as day, or catch a glimpse of a shadow or figure out of the corner of my eye, and when I look properly there’s no one there. My wife says I sometimes shout or sit up looking terrified, but I barely remember it.

During the day I feel on edge all the time. Little things set me off—if I hear a loud bang, like a truck backfiring or something heavy dropping, it’s like I’m right back in that building, with the alarms going off and people screaming. Sometimes it’s not even a sound—just walking past a construction site or smelling diesel, and suddenly I’m seeing it again, as if it’s happening in front of me. I hear the metal crashing, people calling for help, and for a few seconds I forget I’m standing on my own street. Once it passes, I know it wasn’t really happening, but in the moment it feels completely real. I don’t feel like people are out to get me or anything like that—it’s just that accident replaying itself in my head and my ears, over and over.
